problem: Which of the following describes the level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{\operatorname{arcsin}⁡z}{x+y}?$

choices.value: A family of surfaces given by $z=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(c(x+y))$

examples.knowledge_point: Describing a Level Surface of a Function
examples.problem: Find the family of surfaces that describe the level surfaces of the function $f(x,y, z) = \ln(x^2 + 2y^2 - z^2).$
examples.worked_solution:
The level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}) & =c \\ {x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}-{z}^{2} & ={e}^{c} \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{{e}^{c}}+\frac{2{y}^{2}}{{e}^{c}}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{{e}^{c}} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get a family of hyperboloids of one sheet:

$$
\dfrac{x^2}{e^c} + \dfrac{y^2}{e^c/2} - \dfrac{z^2}{e^c} =  1, \qquad c \in (-\infty,\infty)
$$

feedback.problem: For the function $f(x,y,z)=z-4{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}+1,$ find the equation of the level surface $f(x,y,z)=1.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The level surfaces for the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the equation

$$
f(x,y,z)=c.
$$

In our case, we're interested in $c=0.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ z-4{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}+1 & =1 \\ z & =4{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the level surface for $c=1$ is the elliptic paraboloid $z=4{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}.$
